$comment: The source of sf-header-site's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), in the 1.4 form (scripts/generate-component-files.mjs writes rule.js, aliases.json, studio.fixture.json, studio.scenario.json, probe.json and smart.manifest.json from it). A new component, made against standard simai.smart-component 1.3.11 and vocabulary 1.1.5; the brief is ui-control's site-header design brief of 2026-10-28.

collapse.summary: Below this Framework breakpoint (sm 32rem, md 44rem, lg 60rem, xl 72rem) the nav and the actions leave the bar for the side panel and the menu button appears; always: the panel at every width; none: never. A media rule, so the first paint is right without the script

menu-placement.summary: The side of the collapsed bar's menu button and of its side panel (C104): inline-start, the button first in the bar and the panel from the start edge; inline-end, the button last, after the tools, and the panel from the end edge. The two always share a side; a right-to-left page mirrors both

sticky.summary: The bar stays at the top of the window while the page scrolls; flat at the top of the page, it takes the raised shadow while content runs under it (host state data-scrolled)

size.summary: The ladder rung of the bar's controls: the bar's height follows it, and the menu and close buttons take it. Slotted controls are given the same size by the page

navigation-align.summary: Where the nav stands in the wide bar: start, right after the brand; center, at the centre of the bar between the brand and the actions and tools -- the bar's true centre while both sides fit, otherwise the centre of the room left, never over them. Collapsed, the nav is in the side panel either way

label.summary: The side panel's heading and accessible name; «Меню» / «Menu» in the page language when not set (C30: the panel is the phone menu)

menu-label.summary: The menu button's name; «Открыть меню» / «Open menu» in the page language when not set

close-label.summary: The panel's close button's name; «Закрыть меню» / «Close menu» in the page language when not set

open.summary: The side panel is about to open: a request a page may cancel

opened.summary: The side panel opened; a page that fills the sheet slot late does it here

close.summary: The side panel is about to close, and why: its close button, Escape, a press on the scrim, or the action (a link chosen in the panel and a window widened past the breakpoint say api)

closed.summary: The side panel closed, and why

open.summary: Opens the side panel; refused while the bar is not collapsed, or when a page cancels sf-site-header-open

close.summary: Closes the side panel; refused when it is closed already or a page cancels sf-site-header-close

toggle.summary: Opens the side panel when it is closed and closes it when it is open

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The element draws a <header>, the page's banner landmark when it stands outside article, aside, main, nav and section. The navigation landmark is the page's own <nav aria-label> in the nav slot. The menu button is the native button of the sf-icon-button it draws, with aria-haspopup dialog, aria-controls and aria-expanded; the open panel is a dialog named by its heading.

x-summary: The top bar of a SIMAI site: brand, navigation, actions and tools in one row on the container's width, collapsing below a Framework breakpoint into a menu button that opens the navigation and actions as a side panel in the shared layer stack. Every SIMAI site uses it: the effects catalogue, Docara documentation sites and the simai.io hub.

x-source.brief: simai/ui-control site-header design brief, 2026-10-28 (owner approved one shared site header; dispatcher decisions: name sf-site-header, sticky off, collapse lg, no footer, no product switcher)

x-decisions: name: sf-site-header (dispatcher, owner-delegated, 2026-10-28). A leaf with slots: its content is the page's, drawn with Framework components (sf-menu, sf-button-group theme-switch, sf-color, sf-button), so it owns no bus and no rules.

layer: kind panel, locks-page, traps-focus (§19.1), registered in the shared layer stack of core/js/layer-stack.js the way sf-drawer registers -- openLayer with locksPage (the stack's default page lock, lockPageScroll), root, focusIn, onEscape, onTab and place; closeLayer, then returnLayerFocus. No overlay system of its own: the stack orders it, hands it Escape and Tab only while it is the top layer, holds the one page lock and gives focus back.

sheet: the panel is the header's own element, not a portal and not an sf-drawer. Wide, the panel is display: contents, so the nav and the actions stand in the row; collapsed and closed it is not shown; collapsed and open it is a fixed side panel at the inline start with a scrim. The page's nav and actions nodes are placed once and never move or get copied (§4.5): one nav in the page, its listeners and state kept. sf-drawer was the other option; it collects its children as content, so the nav would have had to move between the bar and the drawer on every width change.

collapse: a ladder step, not a length, so the switch is one media rule per step in the sheet: the first paint is right without the script and nothing is measured. A measured auto mode was left out: it decides after layout and would move the first paint (gate 24).

reason: the close event keeps §19.3's closed list. A link chosen in the panel and a window widened past the breakpoint close it with api; the brief's navigate and resize would be vocabulary additions, not made here.
values: none. open is the host state data-open (as sf-help-mark), not a value: a value open would collide with the action open.

nav slot: the default slot. Children without a slot attribute are the navigation: a <nav aria-label> with a list of links, or sf-menu orientation=horizontal collapse=none, which the header turns vertical while the bar is collapsed (its public orientation setting, never its look).

geometry (docs/foundation-composition-geometry.md): the bar is the size's control height plus a space-1 inset above and below plus the 1px region edge; the brand mark is the size 1/2 control height; gutters are the .container's, so a product's --sf-container-gutter reaches the bar; every length is a token.

css-variables: eight public variables (§6), listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json. The Framework never sets one, so the bar's height a page reads is the internal --sf-site-header--block-size the sheet computes.
words (§11): label, menu-label and close-label default to the language files' runtime words.

version 1.1.0: navigation-align (owner decision by recommendation, 2026-11-01), start (the default, the 1.0 bar) or center, the nav of a Docara-like header. A sheet rule, nothing measured, so the first paint is right without the script: the brand and the end of the bar (the tools; the actions and the tools when there are actions) share the room the nav leaves, each at least its own width, so the nav stands at the bar's true centre while both sides fit and moves aside rather than overlap them; with actions the nav is centred in the room between the brand and the actions. Collapsed, nothing changes: the nav is in the side panel. The same at size 1/2 and 1.

version 1.2.3: collapse reads its step from core/js/breakpoints.js (SF.breakpoints, core.runtime 1.20.0), the ladder the sheet switches at, instead of a copy of it (reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 6). The same steps.

version 1.3.0: the tag is sf-header-site (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.header-site and the bundle cl-header-site follow it. sf-site-header stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-header-site, sf-site-header) (change journal tag-sf-site-header-to-sf-header-site, path-smart-site-header-to-header-site).
version 1.3.1: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.

version 1.3.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.0 (one number above the unreleased 1.3.3, on two branches, and 1.4.0 it joins): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; the examples' theme switch is sf-segmented without appearance (the track is its default since sf-segmented 1.4.0). The bar itself is unchanged.

version 1.5.0 background-color-names: the public variable --sf-site-header-background-color (C16 naming: a variable that sets a colour ends in -color, as the other 53 do). The former name --sf-site-header-background is still read under the new one until 2027-01-01 (change journal token-component-background-color-names, src/core/contracts/token-aliases.v1.json); nothing draws differently.

version 1.6.1: a sticky bar is the flat place at the top of the page and the raised one while content runs under it (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08): the host state data-scrolled (a passive scroll listener while sticky is on) gives the bar --sf-shadow-raised and, in the dark theme, the raised surface; a colour the page set stays. The side panel is the modal place: --sf-shadow-modal on --sf-surface-popup over the shared scrim, black 64. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives the action's method its one object argument, close({reason}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.2 (2026-11-09): the menu panel declares a popup place (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08). Also: a patch, the collapsed bar fits its width. The brand gives way (flex 0 1 auto) and its slot content may close down (min-inline-size 0 at no weight), so a phone bar whose brand and tools are wider than it shrinks the brand to the page's own ellipsis instead of scrolling the page sideways (ui-doc home at 390: 10 px sideways, the language button the extra tool). The wide bar, settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.8.0 (2026-11-09, owner decision C30, the site row's line on the bar's edge): a minor, an addition. The nav slot takes the row's whole height (its content stays on the centre line) and publishes the bar's edge as --sf-site-header--edge: how far below the nav's end the bar's bottom border ends (the row's padding, space-1, and the border, px). sf-menu's row lays its current section's 2 px line on that border, as the tabs do; nothing else in the bar moves. The side panel's default heading is «Меню» / «Menu» (was «Навигация» / «Navigation»), as C30's phone menu names it; a label set by the author is kept.

version 1.8.1 (2026-11-10, pair ui-a0370c0c99fb acceptance, D1): a patch. The page's slot nodes (the named slots and the nav) stay where the page wrote them until the bar draws, and the drawing takes them out and places them in the same task (static holdsSlotNodesUntilDrawn, core.runtime 1.50.0). They were out of the document from the bar's connection to its first drawing, one or more tasks, and a page that found its sf-menu by id once sf-menu was defined got null on 8 of 20 loads (prototypes/menu-simple.html, the phone tree). Beside a printed first paint they stay held out of view (data-sf-held). Settings, values, events, keys and the drawing unchanged; tests/browser/header-site-slot-in-document.browser.mjs.

version 1.8.1 also carries C43 in its built sheet (2026-11-10, pair next integration): as a place (sf-place) it takes back --sf-surface-underlay with one line, --sf-surface-underlay: initial; nothing is drawn differently outside a selected row.

version 1.8.2 (2026-11-10, C16 leftovers; written as a note on 1.8.1, which is released): a patch; nothing draws differently. Its sheet reads the C16 role name --sf-surface-page where it read the former --sf-surface-0 (an alias of it until 2027-01-01, token-c16-theme-role-names), so a page that sets the new name reaches it; the value is the same in both themes and on every place. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.8.3 (2026-11-11): a patch: the class button-group sheet its tools draw with changed (component.button-group 1.3.0, C47), and the catalogue example names its colour with aria-label (sf-input-color 1.6.0 draws label visibly).

version 1.8.4 (2026-11-12, R189 MP-3): a patch. The side panel's close button stands on the menu button's axis, as the sheet always said: it is drawn first in the panel's head, at the bar's own gutter (the .container steps of the row, or --sf-container-gutter when a product sets it), the heading after it. It stood at the head's far end, 291 px from the menu button's axis in a 390 window. The DOM order is unchanged (heading, then close), so the first-paint markup and what a reader hears are the same. Settings, values, slots, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.9.0 (2026-11-12, owner decision C104, R189 MP-1, MP-2, MP-6 and the wide-window rest of MP-3): a minor, additions. (1) menu-placement inline-start (the default, the bar as before) or inline-end: the menu button is the bar's last item, after the tools, and the side panel comes from the end edge; its close button stands at the end of the head, on the button's axis. (2) A switch of the page's own opens the panel, as sf-drawer's data-drawer: an element with data-header-site="toggle", "open" or "close" naming the bar's id in aria-controls. The bar keeps the switch's aria-expanded, and while a toggle or open switch outside the panel is on screen it draws no menu button of its own (checked after each drawing and on resize; focus goes back to the switch). (3) MP-6: while open, the scrim and the panel stand above everything in the bar: they take --sf-z-index-1 inside the bar's stacking context, and the brand, the tools and the menu button are isolated, so a z-index inside them (sf-button's text, z-index 1) stays under the scrim; closed, nothing is isolated, so a menu that drops from the tools is not capped. (4) MP-3 in a wide window: the panel's head adds the row's centring offset, half of what the page is wider than the row's container step (the page width as the container breakout reads it), so with collapse always the close stands on the menu button's axis at 1440 too; it is held inside the panel when the offset is wider than the panel. Slots, events, keys and the first paint of a bar without these settings unchanged.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-header-site as the top bar of every public SIMAI site: brand, navigation, actions and tools, with a side panel on a narrow screen.
do_not: Do not draw a header of your own on a SIMAI site
Do not set the bar's colours, height or gutters per site; a product sets --sf-container-gutter once for the page
Do not put a second <nav> around the nav slot; the page's own <nav aria-label> is the landmark
